about: I’m a full-stack developer working on an enterprise healthcare product: electronic health records, billing, procurement, inventory and the workflow engine that ties them together.
Most of my work is turning detailed business rules into services and screens that behave predictably: clear APIs, careful validation and permissions, and data that stays consistent across modules.
Alongside product work, I build the AI-assisted developer platform my team uses to plan, fix, migrate and test code, with approval gates and read-only access to production data built in.

caseStudies.title: Workflow engine
caseStudies.summary: The engine that runs configurable business processes and approvals across the platform.
caseStudies.challenge: Hospital operations depend on multi-step processes, such as approvals and hand-offs between departments, that differ from one customer to the next. Hard-coding each one doesn’t scale.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on the workflow engine that executes configurable processes, including sequential and parallel execution, state transitions and approval flows.
highlights: Configurable processes and approval flows instead of hard-coded steps.
Sequential execution, where each step starts only after the previous one finishes.
Parallel execution, where independent steps run together and the workflow continues once they have all finished.
Explicit state transitions so every workflow instance is always in a known state.

points.text: Order is guaranteed, so a step can rely on the output of the one before it. It’s simpler to reason about and recover, but the total time is the sum of every step.
Independent steps run at the same time, which shortens the overall flow. In exchange, the engine has to join the branches, decide what happens when one fails, and keep shared state consistent.
Steps with data dependencies stay sequential; independent approvals or notifications can branch. Making that a configuration choice keeps the engine general.

caseStudies.title: Procurement management
caseStudies.summary: The purchasing lifecycle, from request for quotation to rate contracts and approvals.
caseStudies.challenge: Hospital purchasing runs through several stages and approvals, and each stage feeds stock, billing and accounts downstream.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on procurement capabilities across the purchasing lifecycle.
highlights: Request for quotation (RFQ) and quotation management.
Rate contracts for agreed supplier pricing.
Approval workflows built on the platform’s workflow engine.
Integration with inventory so purchases flow into stock.

caseStudies.title: Inventory management
caseStudies.summary: Stock, items and unit conversions, with indent and return flows connected to procurement.
caseStudies.challenge: Items are bought in one unit and issued in another, and stock moves between stores and departments. Quantities have to stay correct at every step.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on inventory operations and their integration with procurement and other modules.
highlights: Stock and item management.
Unit-of-measure conversions between purchase and issue units.
Indent (internal request) and return flows.
Integration with procurement, billing and clinical modules, including consumption of non-stock items.

caseStudies.title: Billing & advance management
caseStudies.summary: Billing, patient advances and refunds, with permission-based limits and validation.
caseStudies.challenge: Billing touches money and many modules at once. Every transaction has to be validated, permitted for the user making it, and consistent with the rest of the system.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on billing and advance-management flows.
highlights: Billing workflows and invoice generation.
Advance management: collecting, tracking and applying patient advances.
Refund handling with permission-based limits.
Validation of financial transactions and role-based access through Spring Security.

caseStudies.title: Accounts & financial workflows
caseStudies.summary: Accounting-related workflows connected to billing and day-to-day operations.
caseStudies.challenge: Financial records have to reflect what billing and operations actually did, under the business rules finance teams rely on.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on accounting-related workflows and their integration with billing and enterprise operations.
highlights: Financial processing that applies the platform’s business rules.
Integration with billing and other enterprise modules.

caseStudies.title: Clinical EHR platform
caseStudies.summary: Electronic health record workflows for doctors and nurses across every care setting.
caseStudies.challenge: Clinical screens have to fit very different settings (outpatient, inpatient, emergency and daycare) and roles, while enforcing what must be recorded.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on clinical workflows and their configuration across care settings.
highlights: OPD, IPD, emergency and daycare workflows.
Clinical casesheets and dashboards for doctors and nurses.
Medication and eMAR (electronic medication administration record) workflows.
Role-based access, configurable components with inherited configuration, and mandatory-field validation.
Integrations with other clinical services.

caseStudies.title: Upload engine
caseStudies.summary: A shared framework for uploading, validating and processing files across modules.
caseStudies.challenge: Many modules need bulk data and document uploads. A shared framework avoids each module reinventing validation, storage and error reporting.
caseStudies.contribution: Worked on the platform’s core upload framework.
highlights: One upload framework reused across modules instead of one per module.
Validation and error handling for uploaded data before it is processed.

toolkit.title: Engineering Toolkit · Preetham ND
toolkit.description: Preetham ND's Enterprise AI Platform: Claude Code commands, agents and read-only MCP integrations that help an engineering team plan, fix, migrate and test code with approval gates.
toolkit.intro: I build and maintain an AI developer platform that my team uses with Claude Code, the Claude desktop app and other coding assistants. It turns everyday engineering jobs into repeatable commands with the same rules every time.

principles.title: Approval before change
principles.text: Every command that edits code or data stops for a human go-ahead first. Skipping the gate is an explicit opt-in.

principles.title: Read-only by default
principles.text: Integrations with databases, the issue tracker, source control, logs and metrics are read-only. Data fixes are written as scripts for review, never run.

principles.title: Load only what’s needed
principles.text: Coding standards, rules and domain knowledge are loaded on demand for the task at hand instead of all at once.

principles.title: One source of truth
principles.text: A single command registry drives every assistant integration, and CI rejects commands that are referenced but not defined.

principles.title: Portable core
principles.text: Company-specific knowledge sits behind one profile file, so the core can be reused by another team.

principles.title: Knowledge-graph first
principles.text: Agents ask a code knowledge graph for flows, usages and impact before scanning source files.

items.name: Bug fix
items.text: Root-causes a defect from a ticket, stack trace, log or screenshot and proposes a fix for approval.

items.name: New development
items.text: Designs and implements features from a story, document or screenshot.

items.name: AI developer agent
items.text: Executes a written plan or spec end to end: analyse, plan, execute, validate, fix. Single- or multi-agent.

items.name: Migration
items.text: Moves a change between branches or releases, either as the smallest exact diff or as the full capability.

items.name: UI design update
items.text: Fixes UI bugs or applies design changes while preserving Angular bindings or Flutter widget structure.

items.name: Planning
items.text: Turns a story or bug report into a technical plan and a test-case sheet.

items.name: Plan reviewer
items.text: Scores a plan against real evidence (code, database, logs, metrics, events, requirements) and only approves it when every score clears the bar.

items.name: Bulk issue report
items.text: Summarises a list of tickets with status and evidence-backed root causes. Read-only.

items.name: Test
items.text: Detects the test stack, reports coverage gaps for a change and scaffolds the missing tests.

items.name: Data correction
items.text: Analyses data issues and writes correction scripts for manual review. It never runs them.

items.name: Prompt audit
items.text: Scores prompts against the CRISP framework and suggests a tighter rewrite.

items.name: Knowledge capture
items.text: Records what was learned during a task so later agents can reuse it.

items.name: Usage report
items.text: Summarises prompt and session history with quality scoring.
